scope: Algebraic semantic-token resolutions shared by all lowering backends. Rules select value/effect/context shapes; route IDs are forbidden.

conformanceVocabulary.scope: Authenticated context and target-availability vocabulary for the generated conformance plan. Rows select declaration shapes, never inferred platform-name substrings.

fallback.targetReason: platform-gated API has no authenticated target-availability row

selectorLanguage.overlap: Two matching rules may not resolve the same token for one unit

measuredFields.note: `linkage` and `availabilityKinds` are categories of MEASUREMENT, not names. They are the answers scripts/generate-dmsdk-symbol-evidence.mjs read out of the engine archives the pinned engine/defoldsdk.zip says Extender links, per bundle target and per build variant. Selecting on them states which evidence a rule needs, and a declaration the evidence does not cover matches no rule and stays blocked.

linkage.external: an externally visible definition exists in a linked engine archive
linkage.header-only: inline or static, so no external symbol exists by design
linkage.absent: the archives were asked for every target and none defines it
linkage.unmeasured: clang named no symbol for it, so the archives were never asked

availabilityKinds.all-targets-all-variants: defined for every bundle target under every build variant
availabilityKinds.header-only: no symbol is needed for any target or variant
availabilityKinds.target-subset: defined for some bundle targets and measurably not for others
availabilityKinds.variant-conditional: the debug, release and headless link lines do not agree
availabilityKinds.partially-measured: at least one bundle target could not be asked
availabilityKinds.unmeasured: no bundle target could be asked

rules.scope: Linkage is answered when a linked engine archive defines the symbol the declaration denotes.
rules.rationale: The token was added to every dmSDK unit before any declaration was examined, so it recorded our not having looked rather than anything about the API. llvm-nm over defoldsdk/lib/<dir> - restricted to the engineLibs the SDK's own extender/build.yml names for that platform, edited by the SDK's own variant appmanifest - answers it declaration by declaration, matching the compiler's own mangled name for each target's ABI.

rules.scope: Linkage is answered when the declaration is inline or static and therefore emits no external symbol.
rules.rationale: An inline or static declaration is absent from every archive BY DESIGN, and our bindings are C++ that Extender compiles, so it is reached through the thunk already emitted rather than by linking. Treating that absence as a missing symbol would block the one case where there is nothing to miss.

rules.scope: The target/variant availability matrix is answered when the measurement agrees across all of them.
rules.rationale: The token stood at 'unverified-all-targets' for every unit, which is a statement about the census rather than the API. It is now measured over all 12 bundle targets and all 3 build variants Defold ships an appmanifest for. This rule resolves only the uniform answers: a declaration that is target-conditional, variant-conditional, unlinked, or that some target could not be asked about, matches no rule and stays blocked, because those are real findings rather than missing work.

rules.scope: Call-thread affinity is a property of OUR calling context, and our calling context has one thread.
rules.rationale: The token was read as a question about each native API's thread-safety, which no census can answer from a header. The answerable question is which thread we call FROM. The extension spawns no threads - there is no std::thread, no pthread_create and no dmThread::New anywhere in defold/defold_hermes/src - and every binding call enters through UpdateLuaInstance (a Lua callback), through UpdateExtension, or through the Initialize/Finalize and AppInitialize/AppFinalize extension lifecycle, all of which Defold runs on the main thread. The callback_lifecycle_registry already enforces this, rejecting any operation that arrives on a thread other than its owner's. This resolution says nothing about a native callback being INVOKED on another thread; that is callback-thread-reentrancy-lifetime, which stays unresolved.
